title: Hardening roundup and triage notes - 2026-09-15
content:
Attendees: Maya (chair), Liam, Sofia, Rajiv, Claire, plus SRE on rotation (Devon)

Purpose: quick weekly synth for security engineering: surface high-priority vuln triage items, secrets findings, and next round of threat-modeling checkpoints for upcoming infra changes. Keep decisions lightweight and capture owners.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Prioritized patching window for CUDA kernel CVE (see JIRA-SEC-4127) scheduled for 09/22; Dedicated pools will be live-migrated per rollout plan. Owner: Rajiv.
- Secrets scanning: new high-confidence leakage in a historical repo (archive) flagged and remediated; still need org-wide rotate of the service token used by platform-health. Owner: Sofia.
- Threat modeling kickoff for private-deployments v2 (customer-managed HSM option) scheduled 09/21; pre-read and questionnaire live. Owner: Claire.
- Short-term mitigations: deploy iptables ruleset refinement to block suspicious control-plane probes; SRE/infra to validate no customer-facing regressions. Owner: Liam + Devon.

Notes by topic:

1) Vulnerability triage roundup
- New items this week:
  * CVE candidate: GPU driver interaction causing unbounded memory growth under certain model-serve workloads. Root cause likely in third-party kernel module; reproducible on rtx-8000 test harness. Tracked as JIRA-SEC-4127. Impact: possible DOS for Dedicated GPU pools.
  * Container escape report from fuzzing harness (low severity). Sandbox patch available upstream; needs regression test added to release pipeline.

- Discussion:
  * Rajiv: recommend staged rollout for driver patch on Dedicated hosts only for initial validation; do not push to hosted-api until patch telemetry stable for 48h.
  * Maya: confirm rollback plan and capacity fallback (route to smaller-model CPU fallback pool) in case of regression.

- Decisions / Actions:
  * Action: Rajiv to own patch coordination with infra and schedule maintenance window 2026-09-22 02:00-04:00 UTC. Follow-up: post-mortem if incidents observed. (owner: Rajiv, due: 2026-09-22)
  * Action: Add regression test for container escape to CI (owner: Liam, due: 2026-09-29)

2) Secrets scanning and remediation
- Observations:
  * TruffleHog scan surfaced a high-confidence API key in an archived config repo (internal sandbox). Key was issued 2024-11 and has low usage, but scope includes platform-health reporting.
  * Immediate remediation performed: key revoked and rotated for platform-health. However, token appears embedded in an old deploy script that is still referenced by one historic CI job.

- Discussion:
  * Sofia: we need a focused runbook for historical repos. Many scans flag low-risk items where keys are already expired; but those that are active should be triaged faster.
  * Devon: propose tagging scanned items with "requires-rotate", "requires-audit", "archived-no-action" to reduce noise.

- Decisions / Actions:
  * Action: Sofia to produce a 1-page runbook for archived-repo secret handling and a short regex whitelist for allowed patterns in archives. (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-09-20)
  * Action: Add job to platform CI to detect references to revoked tokens and fail vintage CI jobs that still execute archive scripts (owner: Claire + CI infra, due: 2026-09-30)

3) Threat modeling: private-deployments v2 (HSM option)
- Context: Product is adding a customer-managed HSM integration and a new private control plane mode. Need to re-run threat model focusing on key lifecycle, trust boundaries, and supply-chain dependencies (HSM drivers/firmware).

- Pre-read status:
  * Draft questionnaire sent to eng and product, checklist items include: key provisioning flow, compromise scenarios, firmware upgrade policy, remote attestation model.

- Discussion:
  * Claire: prioritize compromise scenarios where a midstream orchestration host is compromised and has visibility into customer key operations.
  * Rajiv: ensure the model includes an offline key-escrow option and explicit operator-only key rotation UI flows.

- Decisions / Actions:
  * Action: Threat modeling workshop scheduled 2026-09-21 16:00 UTC. Pre-work: all attendees must complete the questionnaire and pin answers in Confluence page CONFLUENCE-SEC/hardening-playbook-v2. (owner: Claire, due: 2026-09-20)
  * Action: Sofia to draft proposed minimum HSM firmware attestation checklist for legal/compliance review. (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-09-28)

4) Observability and alerting adjustments
- Current gap: alerts for suspicious control-plane probe patterns are noisy and not tuned for new telemetry emitted by the serving runtime. This increases mean time to detect real probing attempts.

- Discussion:
  * Liam: put a 2-week observability sprint to (a) add sample probes to test harness, (b) tune thresholding to percentile-based heuristics, (c) add an enrichment pipeline to correlate control-plane probes with recent config changes.

- Decisions / Actions:
  * Action: Liam to scope sprint and propose alert tuning changes; include runbook snippets for SOC. (owner: Liam, due: 2026-09-23)

5) On-call handoff notes / playbook updates
- Reminder: new on-call rotation includes a dedicated security-engineering pager during maintenance windows for Dedicated fleet activities.
- Action: Maya to publish a short maintenance playbook (step-by-step) for dedicated-maintenance windows, include safe rollback commands and traffic routing shortcuts. (owner: Maya, due: 2026-09-18)

Open questions / risks:
- Do we have a clear fallback capacity plan if the GPU driver patch causes regressions for hosted customers? (Rajiv to confirm by 09/20)
- Are archived repos adequately covered by legal hold policies if they contain customer data? Need legal check on archive retention. (Maya to loop in Legal, due: 2026-09-22)
- HSM firmware supply chain: who will own firmware signing verification? Need to decide between Product Security vs. Platform Security. (Discuss in threat modeling workshop)

Quick wins identified:
- Tagging scanned secrets with triage labels to reduce noise (fast): implement in next TruffleHog run.
- Add a short CI gate to fail legacy archive jobs that use revoked tokens.

Meeting artifacts and references:
- Playbook draft: CONFLUENCE-SEC/hardening-playbook-v2
- JIRA: JIRA-SEC-4127 (CUDA driver memory growth)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/sec-tooling/pull/89 (secrets scan tags PR)

Notes / freeform (raw capture):
- "Need to reconcile 'archived-no-action' semantics: sometimes an archive still houses a proof-of-concept infra script that gets occasionally re-run by an old cronjob — so 'archive' != 'dead'." — Claire
- "If driver patch can't be validated in hosted-api quickly, pre-stage fallback containers with older runtime that avoid the problematic kernel path." — Rajiv

Next sync: 2026-09-22 09:30 UTC (short standup focused on patch rollout readiness)

End of notes.
